findings.desc: codex host-2: sanitizeNestedDetails (codex-cli.ts:122-129) copies EVERY own key of prompt_tokens_details, not only the adapter-read cached_tokens. A real payload prompt_tokens_details:{cached_tokens:1, transcript:"secret"} surfaces the nested non-token key transcript in reportedUsage, violating the story's token-only projection contract. This is an own-key leak (NOT prototype pollution) so it triggers on a plain provider response. The OpenAI adapter reads ONLY prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens (adapters/openai.ts:84), so the nested projection must whitelist exactly cached_tokens.

codex host-2: the usage-shape predicates isCodexUsageObject (codex-cli.ts:99) and isGeminiUsageObject (gemini-cli.ts:~102) still use prototype-chain `in` reads. With Object.prototype.prompt_tokens (or promptTokenCount) polluted, an empty own {usage:{}} matches as a valid usage object, so extractCodexUsage/extractGeminiUsage select it, project an empty null-proto object, and STOP before a later real usage line. Repro (codex-verified): pollute Object.prototype.prompt_tokens, stdout "{usage:{}}\n{usage:{prompt_tokens:10,completion_tokens:2}}" returns keys [] instead of the real counts. This defeats the extractCodexUsage ownProp guard at codex-cli.ts:189. Fix: the predicates must use own-property checks (ownProp) to stay consistent with the in-scope extractor hardening.

codex host-2: the smoke does not exercise (a) a nested non-token key under prompt_tokens_details being dropped from the projected reportedUsage (the bug above), nor (b) the false-positive `in`-predicate case where a polluted Object.prototype token key makes an empty first usage object suppress a later real usage line. Add both cases for codex and (for the predicate case) gemini.
